html:
Grantley Adams was a Barbadian lawyer who founded the Barbados Labour Party in 1938 and led the island's move to self rule. He was the only prime minister of the West Indies Federation, from 1958 to 1962.

After the riots of 1937, which followed the expulsion of the labour organiser Clement Payne, Adams built the party and the Barbados Workers' Union. He won reforms for workers and the vote for all adults in 1950, and became the island's first premier.

The federation failed when Jamaica voted to leave, and his rival Errol Barrow led Barbados to independence. His son Tom Adams was prime minister in the 1970s and 1980s, part of the Commonwealth Caribbean's long labour tradition.
